target_customer: Urban millennial and Gen Z consumers in Nigerian cities outside Lagos, plus restaurants that use its ordering software
problem: Restaurants in secondary Nigerian cities were underserved by delivery platforms; Heyfood delivers meals and sells restaurants ordering and delivery software.
business_model: Marketplace delivery fees and commissions, plus SaaS for restaurants

founders.name: Taiwo Akinropo
education: Computer Science (school not named on YC page)
previous_startups: Social discovery platform for students launched in college

founders.name: Demilade Odetara
founders.background_notes: Software and platform engineer at Nigerian tech companies per YC page.

competitors.name: Jumia Food
competitors.what: Food delivery marketplace operating in Lagos, Ibadan, Abuja and Port Harcourt

competitors.name: Glovo
competitors.what: Spanish on-demand delivery platform about to launch in Nigeria

technical_complexity.rationale: Ordering app, dispatch and restaurant software are standard; the challenge is operations in cities with weak logistics.

defensibility.rationale: Local rider and restaurant networks in underserved cities help, but software is copyable and larger players had cash.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Jumia Food closed in December 2023 and Bolt Food left Nigeria that month per press, which cleared space; Heyfood announced expansion to Abuja and Benin in 2024.

market_need_then: Nigeria had millions of young urban professionals and active delivery platforms in Lagos; the company projects a 51B market but that is its own claim.

identity.logo: White circle icon on the app site

branding.community_and_virality: Press on expansion in TechCabal; a campus origin story and 100k users in 5 cities claim appears in one blog headline (not verified).

brand_strength.rationale: Friendly easy name but generic, with little brand press.

outcome_analysis: Heyfood focused on Ibadan and other cities outside contested Lagos, raised a seed from YC, Voltron, Goodwater and Ventures Platform, and was expanding to Abuja and Benin in 2024 with about 40 staff. Jumia Food and Bolt Food exited Nigeria in December 2023, which helped. Funding size is unverified, so capital strength is unknown.
notes: TechCabal reports an undisclosed seed from the listed investors. Aggregators give 500K (Dealroom, StartupBlink), about 1M (Caplight) and 130K (Liners); unverified so amount is null. Founding year 2022 per YC versus 2021 in Dealroom and Village. Main site fetch showed little information. Exit information: no shutdown or acquisition found.
